FilterTime.description:
A filter's exposure: everything captured, and how much of it is usable or rejected so far. The rest is
still waiting (for calibration or grading).
FilterTime.title: FilterTime

HelperSample.description: CPU and memory of the helper and the tool it's running, shown in Activity like a NAS worker's.
HelperSample.title: HelperSample

RecalChange.description: One session's change, so the choice can be made knowing what changes (002-DR-28).
RecalChange.title: RecalChange

ReconExampleOut.description: What a group's files are, shown by one of them (owner 2026-10-11).
ReconExampleOut.title: ReconExampleOut

info.description: SubStation catalogue, ingest and queue API. Sign in through /_allauth/browser/v1/.
info.title: SubStation API

post.description: Bin files by hand: moved to their library's quarantine where SubStation may delete, else hidden.
Run the daily tidy now: bin long-rejected subs, delete what's past its date.
Queue a build for every raw set of 3+ frames with no master built, queued or running from it.

Say which filter these flats were taken through (a camera with no filter wheel records none, so a Duo NB
night's flats read as plain OSC). Stored as your correction for each flat, which regroups them with flats of
that filter so that filter's lights find them. Clear the box to go back to what the headers say.

get.description:
What is stopping grading (002-DR-02): lights waiting for calibration, per dataset and night, with what
SubStation is looking for.

Datasets whose calibrated subs now match different masters (002 C11): listed on the Calibration screen,
re-calibrated only when you say so on the dataset's Calibration tab.
The darks, biases and flats that would release the lights waiting for calibration, biggest win first.
The darks and biases to shoot, as a NINA sequence file.
Your latest changes, newest first (everyone's, for an admin who asks).

post.description: Group every ungrouped dataset as suggested, creating collections named after their object.

get.description:
Datasets that could join this collection (006-DR-05). Where both sides are plate solved (009 P11) the
ranking is by how much of the reference field they cover, then rotation difference; otherwise by the
distance between median header pointings.
What "Stack combined masters" would use, and the combined masters made so far (latest per filter).

Every dataset's solved field over the reference framing, north up (009 P10/P12, 006-DR-09), each with a
sub's preview placed exactly where it sits on the sky. The reference is the one asked for, else the solved
dataset with the most accepted integration. Mosaic panels come back side by side.

post.description:
Treat other target names as `into` from now on (TestSoulNebula, IC 1848 - Soul Nebula → Soul Nebula), so
their subs share datasets and stack together. Every filter follows. Nothing on disk changes.

get.description: HOO or SHO at 100%, made from the project's combined masters (registered to one framing).

post.description: Make projects for the datasets not in one yet (006-DR-20); rename or regroup them afterwards.
Every rejected sub in the dataset (by the grader or by hand), unless marked Keep.

get.description: 002 C11 / 004 T014: newer calibration is offered, never applied silently to calibrated subs.

post.description:
Re-grade with the current thresholds (003-DR-02): without `confirm`, only say what would change; with it,
queue the re-grade. Human verdicts are kept either way.

get.description:
Masters a session could use instead (002 C10): same camera; darks of the session's exposure (or a bias),
flats of its filter. Age and temperature are shown so the choice is informed.

post.description:
Use these masters for this session only (002-DR-07): pinned so a later rematch keeps them, then the
session is calibrated and graded again. Human verdicts stay.

Say which filter a whole session used (owner 2026-10-10). Stored as
your correction for each sub, so it regroups them into that filter's dataset, finds flats for that filter
and measures them again. Clear the box to go back to what the headers say.

get.description:
Datasets that can be stacked with this one (004 T008): same target, filter, camera and telescope (another
rig name or panel split that grouped them apart).

post.description:
Agree with the automatic grades of flagged subs (spec 016): each becomes your own verdict, the same as
the grade, so it leaves the review list. Subs you already decided are left alone.

get.description: The named objects in a solved sub's field, placed on its preview (009 amendment 2026-10-12).

A small image of any frame for hover previews: its preview, QA thumbnail or built-master preview when one
exists, else drawn from the file once and cached (owner 2026-10-11).
The detected stars for the Stars and FWHM map views (003 G15): positions as fractions of the frame.
The 100% view and aberration inspector (owner 2026-10-10): ready, or being made now (a few seconds).

post.description: Draw the 100% view now (a few seconds), for a sub that doesn't have one.
The next master to post-process, or nothing (204). Also the helper's heartbeat while idle.
Say hello without taking a job: the helper's tools show in Settings.
Record the run: previews, 100% views and measurements are drawn here, as for a run on the NAS.

A run that went wrong. While it has attempts left it goes back in the queue (a dropped connection or a
helper restart shouldn't cost the master its post-processing); after that it fails with the helper's reason.
Progress, and the heartbeat that keeps the job from being taken back.

One stage's linear FITS, streamed to disk beside the master (never held in memory).

A proxy may cut a request off after a minute, so a big stage can come in pieces: each piece says where it
starts (`offset`) and the final one says `last`. Sending a piece again overwrites from its offset, so a
retried piece is harmless. Without `offset` the body is the whole file.

get.description:
Active rules, a page at a time when `limit` is given; counting a rule's files is the slow part, so only the
page's rules are counted (except when sorting by files).

post.description: The files an ignore rule sets aside (e.g. 8-bit captures), into the bin.

get.description:
Totals for what the Library's filters show (006, owner 2026-10-10): lights taken, hours per filter and
rig, how many were kept or rejected, and the average SQM where the capture recorded it.

put.description: Limit the nights a master may calibrate (002 C13); every light is matched again. Empty dates clear it.

get.description: Every light in a dataset on one night at one place, in time order (spec 012): the night page's viewer.
Spec 010: which finishing tools the finisher can run, as it last reported.

post.description: Owner 2026-10-12: paste an RC-Astro activation code here instead of running a command on the finisher.

delete.description: The datasets stay in the collection, just not in a project.

get.description: Items with the group each belongs to; the first of each group carries an example file's values.

Flagged subs (spec 003 A2): rejected, down-weighted or near a threshold, grouped by dataset and night,
newest first. Subs the user already decided are left out.
The same subs /review lists, counted without building them (it's polled by every page).

post.description: A rig named before its first sub arrives (008-DR-09): headers that name its telescope and camera join it.

get.description:
Rigs that are probably one: a camera name that contains the other's, and a telescope name that starts the
same (header strings change between capture software versions).

post.description: Treat this rig's header names as the other rig's from now on, and regroup its subs (no file is touched).
The datasets a grading change would re-grade, and how their verdicts would change (008-DR-04).

get.description:
Where each value the catalogue uses comes from (008-DR-01): header keyword, path pattern or you, with how many
files each one decided.

post.description: Solve every measured light that hasn't been (009 P9): a low-priority job shown in Activity.

get.description:
Two masters side by side (004 T006): integration, subs, stars, sharpness and roundness overall and by region.
Noise is shown but never decides on its own: it depends on integration and on the stretch, not quality alone.
The named objects in a solved master's field, placed on its preview (009 amendment 2026-10-12).
What went into a master and how (004-DR-04).
Spec 010: a master's post-processing runs, newest first, each stage with its tool and reason.

post.description: Spec 010 US3: post-process this master again, from the untouched master, with the current settings.
Redraw this master's stages with its stretch, at 100% too.

get.description: A processed version's linear 32-bit file, to download (spec 010 FR-008, 2026-10-15).
A stage at 100%, drawn with its master's stretch.

put.description: Any signed-in user, viewers too: it changes only how the app looks to them.

post.description:
Place a waiting job just before or after another (005 T008). The queue runs by priority, then by enqueue
time, so the job takes the other's priority and an enqueue time a moment either side of it.

get.description:
The waiting jobs a page at a time, in the order they'll run (owner 2026-10-11: scroll the whole queue);
`kind` keeps one kind of job, named as the queue's chips name them ("Calibrate and grade").
Finished jobs, newest first, a page at a time.
